Implementation details for dart.sh. Current resolve_target section:

```bash
resolve_target() {
 local arg="${1:-}"
 TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
 SOURCE="default"
 if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
   SOURCE="argument"
 elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
   SOURCE="environment"
 fi

 local det found det_sdk det_channel
 det="$(quality_detection)"
 found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
 det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

 if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
   [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
   [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
 fi
 ...
``

Insert between environment and quality workflow:

```bash
 if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
   local vp
   vp="$(repo_version_pin)"
   if [ -n "${vp}" ]; then
     TARGET="${vp}"
     SOURCE="version file"
   fi
 fi

 if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
   [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
   ...
``

Note `local` inside the if — bash allows `local` only in functions; resolve_target IS a function. Fine. But declaring `local vp` inside an if block is fine too.

repo_version_pin():
```bash
repo_version_pin() {
 [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
 awk 'NF { sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[:space:]]+|[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit }' "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}
``
Hmm — awk: for each line, if non-empty, strip comment, trim; if still non-empty print and exit. Careful with sub(/#.*/, "") BEFORE trim — a line `3.13.5 # pinned` → `3.13.5 `. Then trim. Let me write:
```bash
awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[:space:]]+|[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit }'
``
Line "# comment": sub removes all → empty → NF==0 → continue. Blank line: skipped. `3.13.5`: prints.

```bash
# ─ Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ─────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#  toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# plus a loud warning line when the repo has no pin at all (match: no is then
# "nothing to match against"), and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos.
cmd_summary() {
 resolve_target ""
 if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
   echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
   return 0
 fi

 # The repo's pin: version file first (gh-1137 step 1), then the CI workflow
 # line (step 2). Nothing found → none (step 3: stable + warning).
 local pin_kind="version"
 pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
 case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
 if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
   local det found det_sdk det_channel
   det="$(quality_detection)"

```bash
# ─ Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ─────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#  toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# plus a loud warning line when the repo has no pin at all (match: no is then
# "nothing to match against"), and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos.
cmd_summary() {
 resolve_target ""
 if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
   echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
   return 0
 fi

 # The repo's pin: version file first (gh-1137 step 1), then the CI workflow
 # line (step 2). Nothing found → none (step 3: stable + warning).
 local pin_kind="version"
 pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
 case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
 if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
   local det found det_sdk det_channel
   det="$(quality_detection)"
   found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
   det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
   if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
     pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
   elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
     pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
   fi
 fi

 local running effective match
 running="$(installed_version)"
 effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}"
 if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
   echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
   echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
   return 0
 fi
 if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
   if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
 else
   if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
 fi
 echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}
``

{"newText":"# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline

repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"

Down to 3 failures. Let me look at each:

1. "network hicup + MANAGED SDK → the managed bin dir is still registered (behavior preserved)" — REGRESSION of an existing test! The degraded-keep test: `dsRun('', { managedBanner: ..., stubCurlFails: true, trailTarget })` — sandbox has NO pubspec → SOURCE=default... wait — do_install now SKIPS on non-Dart repos when SOURCE=default! The degraded-keep test has no pubspec → skip fires before the degraded-keep branch → trail never registered → trail_hit=0 instead of 1.

Hmm. This is a REAL behavioral conflict: previously, bare `dart.sh` on any repo with an existing install kept it (degraded keep). Now non-Dart repos skip. The test's intent: degraded keep must still register the managed dir. The test sandbox isn't a Dart repo...

Who's right? The test encodes gh-918 behavior for "factory legs on dart repos". The skip is gh-1137's non-Dart optimization. A non-Dart repo has no business having a managed dart... but the pool VM's PERSISTENT HOME could carry a dart installed by ANOTHER (Dart) repo's leg! Pool VMs keep $HOME across jobs (the dart SDK at ~/.dart-sdk persists). A non-Dart leg then: SOURCE=default + non-Dart → skip → fine, it doesn't need dart anyway. The skip is still correct.

But the existing test predates the gate and asserts keep-behavior in a sandbox WITHOUT pubspec. Options:
(a) Update the existing test to add `pubspec: true` — the degraded-keep semantics now only apply to Dart repos (and explicit-target runs).
(b) Move the skip AFTER the degraded-keep/cache-hit branch.

Semantically (b) is better: if a usable SDK is already installed, keep-and-register regardless of repo type (harmless, and preserves the PATH/DART_HOME honesty contract). The skip then only prevents DOWNLOADS, not keep-hits. That keeps the old test green without weakening it, and non-Dart repos still never download. Actually hmm — but then a non-Dart repo WITH a stale managed dart would register dart on the leg PATH — harmless noise.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: cache-hit branch (`have == resolved`) — for SOURCE=default non-Dart: resolved = channel_latest(stable) via curl (network!) — cache.sh's keying calls `dart.sh plan` (no do_install), so no curl there. In do_install, the cache-hit check needs `resolved` — curl fires BEFORE the skip if I move the skip later. Non-Dart repo + network-down → resolved="" → degraded keeps the SDK (exit 0). Network-up → resolved found → if have==resolved → cache hit exit 0 (no download). Either way NO download for non-Dart... unless have != resolved → proceeds to DOWNLOAD. {"newText":"# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer

    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"

{"newText":"# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"

  fi

    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

    cmd_summary
    ;;

    usage
    exit 0

    resolve_target "${CMD}"

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CMD="${1:-}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

case "${CMD}" in
  plan)
    os_arch
    resolve_target "$@"
    print_plan
    ;;
  status)
    echo "installed=$(installed_version)"
    echo "install_dir=${DART_INSTALL_DIR}"
    ;;
  summary)
    # Network-free by contract — never os_arch/channel_latest here.
    cmd_summary
    ;;
  help|-h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    os_arch
    resolve_target "${CMD}"
    do_install
    ;;

Who's right? The test encodes gh-918 behavior for "factory legs on dart repos". The skip is gh-1137's non-Dart optimization. A non-Dart repo has no business having a managed dart... but the pool VM's PERSISTENT HOME could carry a dart installed by ANOTHER (Dart) repo's leg! Pool VMs keep $HOME across jobs (the dart SDK at ~/.dart-sdk persists). A non-Dart leg then: SOURCE=default + non-Dart → skip → fine, it doesn't need dart anyway. The skip is still correct.

But the existing test predates the gate and asserts keep-behavior in a sandbox WITHOUT pubspec. Options:
(a) Update the existing test to add `pubspec: true` — the degraded-keep semantics now only apply to Dart repos (and explicit-target runs).
(b) Move the skip AFTER the degraded-keep/cache-hit branch.

Semantically (b) is better: if a usable SDK is already installed, keep-and-register regardless of repo type (harmless, and preserves the PATH/DART_HOME honesty contract). The skip then only prevents DOWNLOADS, not keep-hits. That keeps the old test green without weakening it, and non-Dart repos still never download. Actually hmm — but then a non-Dart repo WITH a stale managed dart would register dart on the leg PATH — harmless noise.

In do_install, the cache-hit check needs `resolved` — curl fires BEFORE the skip if I move the skip later. Non-Dart repo + network-down → resolved="" → degraded keeps the SDK (exit 0). Network-up → resolved found → if have==resolved → cache hit exit 0 (no download). Either way NO download for non-Dart... unless have != resolved → proceeds to DOWNLOAD. Ugh — then the skip must still guard the download path.

Cleanest semantics: the skip gate blocks the DOWNLOAD, positioned just before it, but AFTER cache-hit/degraded-keep. But the loud warning placement — "before any download so the warning survives a failed transfer" — the warning test asserts warning present on the download-failure path; if warning sits with the skip-gate just before the download, same effect.

The degraded-keep-with-warning test (Dart repo, no pin, managed stable present) expects warning + rc 0: warning fires at gate position (before cache checks) in my current impl. # ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

    cmd_summary

    usage

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CMD="${1:-}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

    cmd_summary
    ;;
  help|-h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;

    os_arch
    resolve_target "${CMD}"
    do_install
    ;;

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CMD="${1:-}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

case "${CMD}" in

    resolve_target "$@"

    # Network-free by contract — never os_arch/channel_latest here.
    cmd_summary
    ;;
  help|-h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    os_arch
    resolve_target "${CMD}"

Down to 3 failures. Let me look at each:

1. "network hicup + MANAGED SDK → the managed bin dir is still registered (behavior preserved)" — REGRESSION of an existing test! The degraded-keep test: `dsRun('', { managedBanner: ..., stubCurlFails: true, trailTarget })` — sandbox has NO pubspec → SOURCE=default... wait — do_install now SKIPS on non-Dart repos when SOURCE=default! The degraded-keep test has no pubspec → skip fires before the degraded-keep branch → trail never registered → trail_hit=0 instead of 1.

Hmm. This is a REAL behavioral conflict: previously, bare `dart.sh` on any repo with an existing install kept it (degraded keep). Now non-Dart repos skip. The test's intent: degraded keep must still register the managed dir. The test sandbox isn't a Dart repo...

Who's right? The test encodes gh-918 behavior for "factory legs on dart repos". The skip is gh-1137's non-Dart optimization. A non-Dart repo has no business having a managed dart... but the pool VM's PERSISTENT HOME could carry a dart installed by ANOTHER (Dart) repo's leg! Pool VMs keep $HOME across jobs (the dart SDK at ~/.dart-sdk persists). A non-Dart leg then: SOURCE=default + non-Dart → skip → fine, it doesn't need dart anyway. The skip is still correct.

But the existing test predates the gate and asserts keep-behavior in a sandbox WITHOUT pubspec. Options:

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CMD="${1:-}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

    cmd_summary
    ;;
  help|-h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;

    resolve_target "${CMD}"
    do_install

# ── Leg-summary line (gh-1137) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Network-free. Prints the ONE line the leg summary carries:
#   toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
# <pin> is the repo's pin (version file first, then the CI workflow's
# sdk:/channel: input); match compares what the leg ACTUALLY runs (the
# installed managed SDK banner) against that pin — a channel pin matches on
# channel identity, a version pin on the full version token. A Dart repo with
# NO pin gets match: no PLUS a loud warning line (ticket step 3); a non-Dart
# repo gets a n/a skip line instead of a fake toolchain claim.
cmd_summary() {
  if [ "$(is_dart_repo)" != "1" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart none (CI: none, match: n/a) — not a Dart repo (no pubspec.yaml); SDK install skipped"
    return 0
  fi

  # Resolve the leg's target exactly like the install path does (same
  # precedence), so the summary describes the toolchain the session runs.
  resolve_target ""

  local pin pin_kind="version" running effective match
  pin="$(repo_version_pin)"
  case "${pin}" in stable|beta|dev) pin_kind="channel" ;; esac
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    local det det_sdk det_channel
    det="$(quality_detection)"
    det="${det#*|}"
    det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
    if [ -n "${det_sdk}" ]; then
      pin="${det_sdk}"; pin_kind="version"
    elif [ -n "${det_channel}" ]; then
      pin="${det_channel}"; pin_kind="channel"
    fi
  fi

  running="$(installed_version)"
  effective="${running:-${VERSION:-${CHANNEL}}}"
  if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
    echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: none, match: no)"
    echo "⚠️ toolchain warning: no Dart SDK pin found (.dart-version or dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — local dart format/analyzer results may differ from CI"
    return 0
  fi
  if [ "${pin_kind}" = "channel" ]; then
    if [ "${CHANNEL}" = "${pin}" ] && [ -n "${running}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  else
    if [ "${running}" = "${pin}" ]; then match="yes"; else match="no"; fi
  fi
  echo "toolchain: dart ${effective} (CI: ${pin}, match: ${match})"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CMD="${1:-}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

    cmd_summary
    ;;

    usage
    exit 0
    ;;

import re, io

TARGETS = [
    ('js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js', "js/pushReworkChanges.js"),

import re, io

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, io

TARGETS = [
    ('js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js', "js/pushReworkChanges.js"),
    ('js/unit-tests/test_developTicketAndCreatePR.js', "js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js"),
]
ENTRY = "'./common/toolchainSummary.js': { withToolchainLine: function(t) { return t; } },"

for path, main in TARGETS:
    with io.open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        lines = f.readlines()
    out = []
    inserted = 0
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        out.append(lines[i])
        if main in lines[i]:
            # find the next makeRequire({ from here
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and 'makeRequire({' not in lines[j]:
                j += 1
            if j < len(lines):
                # insert entry lines right after the makeRequire({ line
                for k in range(i+1, j+1):
                    out.append(lines[k])
                indent = re.match(r'\s*', lines[j]).group(0) + '    '
                out.append(indent + ENTRY + '\n')
                inserted += 1
                i = j
        i += 1
    with io.open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.writelines(out)
    print(path, 'inserted', inserted)
EOF"}

                i = j

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, io

TARGETS = [
    ('js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js', "js/pushReworkChanges.js"),
    ('js/unit-tests/test_developTicketAndCreatePR.js', "js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js"),
]
ENTRY = "'./common/toolchainSummary.js': { withToolchainLine: function(t) { return t; } },"

for path, main in TARGETS:
    with io.open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        lines = f.readlines()
    out = []
    inserted = 0
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        out.append(lines[i])
        if main in lines[i]:
            # find the next makeRequire({ from here
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and 'makeRequire({' not in lines[j]:
                j += 1
            if j < len(lines):
                # insert entry lines right after the makeRequire({ line
                for k in range(i+1, j+1):
                    out.append(lines[k])
                indent = re.match(r'\s*', lines[j]).group(0) + '    '
                out.append(indent + ENTRY + '\n')
                inserted += 1
                i = j
        i += 1
    with io.open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.writelines(out)
    print(path, 'inserted', inserted)
EOF"}

import re, io

TARGETS = [
    ('js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js', "js/pushReworkChanges.js"),

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, io

TARGETS = [
    ('js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js', "js/pushReworkChanges.js"),
    ('js/unit-tests/test_developTicketAndCreatePR.js', "js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js"),
]
ENTRY = "'./common/toolchainSummary.js': { withToolchainLine: function(t) { return t; } },"

for path, main in TARGETS:
    with io.open(path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        lines = f.readlines()
    out = []
    inserted = 0
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        out.append(lines[i])
        if main in lines[i]:
            # find the next makeRequire({ from here
            j = i
            while j < len(lines) and 'makeRequire({' not in lines[j]:
                j += 1
            if j < len(lines):
                # insert entry lines right after the makeRequire({ line
                for k in range(i+1, j+1):
                    out.append(lines[k])
                indent = re.match(r'\s*', lines[j]).group(0) + '    '
                out.append(indent + ENTRY + '\n')
                inserted += 1
                i = j
        i += 1
    with io.open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.writelines(out)
    print(path, 'inserted', inserted)
EOF"}

import re, io

TARGETS = [
    ('js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js', "js/pushReworkChanges.js"),

]
ENTRY = "'./common/toolchainSummary.js': { withToolchainLine: function(t) { return t; } },"

87:| `FLUTTER_VERSION` | `stable` | Flutter SDK for agent work, cached per version (flutter-action). Empty string opts out — pure-Dart targets provision `dart` instead (see `DART_VERSION`) |
88:| `DART_VERSION` | *(auto)* | Dart SDK for legs on Dart repos (gh-918): hosted runner images ship **no** `dart`, and without it a rework leg cannot run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` to see or verify gate violations. `setup/dart.sh [stable\|beta\|dev\|<version>]` resolves the target the way CI does — explicit value, else the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:` inputs in the repo's own quality workflow — installs the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN under `~/.dart-sdk`, and puts it on PATH for the leg session. `DART_VERSION` is a pure input pin: `dart.sh` exports only `DART_HOME`, so a later bare `dart.sh` in the same job still re-resolves the channel (and `setup/cache.sh dart` keys restore/save identically). Dart-repo runners add `bash agents/setup/dart.sh` to `customParams.setupCommands`; the cache key is `DART_CACHE_*` (`setup/cache.sh dart`) |

import re, io

            if lines[j].rstrip().endswith('{'):
                indent = re.match(r'\s*', lines[j+1] if j+1 < len(lines) else lines[j]).group(0)

arguments.content:
### What changed
The fa dev/rework runner now provisions the exact Dart SDK the target repo's CI pins, and every leg summary states which SDK it verified with via a machine-generated `toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` line.

### Key decisions
- `setup/dart.sh` resolution precedence now follows gh-1137: explicit value → `DART_VERSION` → repo `.dart-version` pin → `dart-lang/setup-dart` `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's workflows → stable **with a loud "may differ from CI" warning**; a repo with no `pubspec.yaml` skips the install entirely (no ~215 MB SDK for non-Dart legs).
- New network-free `dart.sh summary` emits the summary line (plus a warning line when the repo has no pin); the match flag compares the installed managed SDK banner against the repo pin — a channel pin matches on channel identity, a version pin on the full token.
- `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` appends the line to the leg summary in both post actions (`developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`); every failure path is a no-op, and non-Dart legs stay clean.
- Runner configs `.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json` / `fa-rework.json` carry `bash setup/dart.sh` in `customParams.setupCommands` so the CI-matching SDK is installed before the CLI agent starts (AC1).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_dartSetup.json          # 54 tests — pin precedence, warning, summary line (AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_toolchainSummary.json   # 14 tests — summary append + runner wiring contracts
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                # full suite, 5499 passed / 0 failed
bash setup/dart.sh summary                            # live: n/a skip on non-Dart repos
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SC[customParams.setupCommands] --> DI["setup/dart.sh (install)"]
  DI --> P{"pin?"}
  P -->|".dart-version"| SDK["install pinned version"]

  P -->|"none"| ST["stable + loud warning"]
  DI --> SDK2["dart on leg PATH — dart --version == CI pin (AC1)"]
  PA["postJSAction"] --> TS["toolchainSummary.withToolchainLine"]
  TS --> S["dart.sh summary (network-free)"]
  S --> RM["outputs/response.md += toolchain: dart v (CI: pin, match: yes/no) (AC2/AC3)"]
```

</details>

{"content":"### What changed
The fa dev/rework runner now provisions the exact Dart SDK the target repo's CI pins, and every leg summary states which SDK it verified with via a machine-generated `toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` line.

### Key decisions
- `setup/dart.sh` resolution precedence now follows gh-1137: explicit value → `DART_VERSION` → repo `.dart-version` pin → `dart-lang/setup-dart` `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's workflows → stable **with a loud "may differ from CI" warning**; a repo with no `pubspec.yaml` skips the install entirely (no ~215 MB SDK for non-Dart legs).
- New network-free `dart.sh summary` emits the summary line (plus a warning line when the repo has no pin); the match flag compares the installed managed SDK banner against the repo pin — a channel pin matches on channel identity, a version pin on the full token.
- `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` appends the line to the leg summary in both post actions (`developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`); every failure path is a no-op, and non-Dart legs stay clean.
- Runner configs `.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json` / `fa-rework.json` carry `bash setup/dart.sh` in `customParams.setupCommands` so the CI-matching SDK is installed before the CLI agent starts (AC1).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_dartSetup.json          # 54 tests — pin precedence, warning, summary line (AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_toolchainSummary.json   # 14 tests — summary append + runner wiring contracts
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                # full suite, 5499 passed / 0 failed
bash setup/dart.sh summary                            # live: n/a skip on non-Dart repos
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SC[customParams.setupCommands] --> DI["setup/dart.sh (install)"]
  DI --> P{"pin?"}
  P -->|".dart-version"| SDK["install pinned version"]
  P -->|"setup-dart sdk: (CI)"| SDK
  P -->|"none"| ST["stable + loud warning"]
  DI --> SDK2["dart on leg PATH — dart --version == CI pin (AC1)"]
  PA["postJSAction"] --> TS["toolchainSummary.withToolchainLine"]
  TS --> S["dart.sh summary (network-free)"]
  S --> RM["outputs/response.md += toolchain: dart v (CI: pin, match: yes/no) (AC2/AC3)"]
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

{"content":"### What changed
The fa dev/rework runner now provisions the exact Dart SDK the target repo's CI pins, and every leg summary states which SDK it verified with via a machine-generated `toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` line.

### Key decisions
- `setup/dart.sh` resolution precedence now follows gh-1137: explicit value → `DART_VERSION` → repo `.dart-version` pin → `dart-lang/setup-dart` `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's workflows → stable **with a loud "may differ from CI" warning**; a repo with no `pubspec.yaml` skips the install entirely (no ~215 MB SDK for non-Dart legs).
- New network-free `dart.sh summary` emits the summary line (plus a warning line when the repo has no pin); the match flag compares the installed managed SDK banner against the repo pin — a channel pin matches on channel identity, a version pin on the full token.
- `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` appends the line to the leg summary in both post actions (`developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`); every failure path is a no-op, and non-Dart legs stay clean.
- Runner configs `.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json` / `fa-rework.json` carry `bash setup/dart.sh` in `customParams.setupCommands` so the CI-matching SDK is installed before the CLI agent starts (AC1).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_dartSetup.json          # 54 tests — pin precedence, warning, summary line (AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_toolchainSummary.json   # 14 tests — summary append + runner wiring contracts
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                # full suite, 5499 passed / 0 failed
bash setup/dart.sh summary                            # live: n/a skip on non-Dart repos
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SC[customParams.setupCommands] --> DI["setup/dart.sh (install)"]
  DI --> P{"pin?"}
  P -->|".dart-version"| SDK["install pinned version"]
  P -->|"setup-dart sdk: (CI)"| SDK
  P -->|"none"| ST["stable + loud warning"]
  DI --> SDK2["dart on leg PATH — dart --version == CI pin (AC1)"]
  PA["postJSAction"] --> TS["toolchainSummary.withToolchainLine"]
  TS --> S["dart.sh summary (network-free)"]
  S --> RM["outputs/response.md += toolchain: dart v (CI: pin, match: yes/no) (AC2/AC3)"]
```

</details>
